findings.title: Unauthenticated arbitrary executor drains any 7702-delegated account
findings.description: execute(Call[]) is external payable with no caller authorization; in an EIP-7702 context it runs arbitrary calls with the delegated account's full balance and approvals.
findings.impact: Any address drains all ETH/tokens from any account that installs OpenDelegate as its 7702 delegate.
findings.rootCause: Universal execute entrypoint without owner/msg.sender check.
findings.recommendation: Require msg.sender == address(this) (validated self-call) or an ECDSA auth over the call batch with a nonce.

findings.title: PerpVault price reports are replayable (empty _checkTime, no nonce)
findings.description: _verify authenticates a signed Report{price,ts} but _checkTime is an empty virtual no-op and there is no nonce or msg.sender binding; historical reports in public calldata are reusable.
findings.impact: Attacker opens at a stale low price and closes at a stale high price, extracting other traders' collateral.
findings.rootCause: Report authentication omits timestamp/nonce validation; _checkTime unimplemented in the deployed contract.
findings.recommendation: Enforce MAX_AGE on r.ts, bind a per-user nonce into the signed payload, and consume report digests.

findings.title: ReplayAdapter releases with no replay protection
findings.description: release() checks verifier sigs over keccak256(abi.encode(to,amount)) but records no processed state and binds no nonce or chainid; Adapter.sol has the processed guard this contract omits.
findings.impact: Any caller replays a signed release repeatedly, sending N x the signed amount out of the adapter until drained; also cross-chain replayable.
findings.rootCause: Missing replay guard / nonce / chain-id binding.
findings.recommendation: Add mapping(bytes32=>bool) processed, include nonce + block.chainid in the digest, set processed before transferring.

findings.title: PackedAdapter digest collision inflates payout
findings.description: digestOf hashes abi.encodePacked(chainid,nonce,amount,recipient) with amount and recipient both dynamic bytes and no delimiter, so the amount/recipient boundary is ambiguous and distinct pairs collide.
findings.impact: Front-running a signed release with a 32-byte padded recipient, an attacker re-splits bytes to set amount = A*2^96 to the same address with the same sigs, over-paying from the adapter.
findings.rootCause: abi.encodePacked over two adjacent dynamic arguments.
findings.recommendation: Use abi.encode (length-prefixed) or hash fixed-width fields (uint256 amount, address recipient).

findings.title: Tier.spend has no access control and no real daily limit
findings.description: spend(to,amount) transfers the contract's own tokens with no caller check; dailyLimit returns BASE for any caller, and there is no timestamp/cumulative-spend state so the 'daily' limit is only a per-call cap.
findings.impact: Anyone drains the Tier wallet in 10e6 increments via repeated spend calls.
findings.rootCause: Missing authorization plus absent daily-window accounting.
findings.recommendation: Restrict spend to owner/authorized agents and track cumulative spend within a rolling 24h window against dailyLimit.

findings.title: Router.pull uses an arbitrary from in transferFrom
findings.description: pull(from,amount) calls token.transferFrom(from, sink, amount) with from unbound and no authorization.
findings.impact: Any third party moves any Router-approver's tokens to the fixed sink at will, stripping approvers of custody/timing control (and losing funds if sink is one-way).
findings.recommendation: Use from = msg.sender, or require explicit per-pull authorization from from.

findings.title: RwaToken transfer check ignores the sender
findings.description: canTransfer(address,to) validates only registry.isVerified(to); the from argument is unused, so sender eligibility is never checked.
findings.impact: A holder whose verification is revoked can still transfer to any verified address, defeating the compliance freeze.

findings.title: Wrapper escapes RWA transfer restrictions
findings.description: wtFUND is a plain ERC20 with no transfer gating; wrapping moves restricted RwaToken value into a freely transferable token.
findings.impact: Restricted exposure circulates to non-verified parties; a non-verified holder unwraps via a verified mule, fully bypassing the identity gate.
findings.rootCause: Wrapped token does not inherit the underlying's transfer restrictions.
findings.recommendation: Apply the registry.isVerified gate to wtFUND transfers, or restrict wrap/unwrap/holding to verified addresses.

findings.title: RedemptionVault never checks NAV staleness or zero
findings.description: _nav() returns feed.nav() with no staleness or non-zero check, despite declared error StaleNAV(), NavFeed.updatedAt, and an unused ref feed.
findings.impact: Redemptions clear at a stale price during feed outages; a zero NAV makes a redeemer surrender shares for 0 USDC.
findings.rootCause: Declared staleness machinery not wired into the redemption path.
findings.recommendation: Require feed.nav() > 0 and block.timestamp - feed.updatedAt() <= MAX_AGE before pricing a redemption.

findings.title: AsyncRedeem settles at a backward-looking NAV
findings.description: requestRedeem stamps the current epoch and settle pays navAt(r.epoch) — the NAV known at request time, with no forward pricing (NotYetPriced declared but unused); settle is permissionless and same-epoch callable.
findings.impact: A holder anticipating a write-down redeems at the current high NAV and exits whole, socializing the loss onto remaining holders.
findings.rootCause: Backward-looking NAV selection instead of forward (next-strike) pricing.
findings.recommendation: Price redemptions at the first NAV struck strictly after the request epoch; reject settle until that strike exists.

findings.title: DelegateA.setOwner unauthenticated; DelegateA/DelegateB share storage slot 0
findings.description: DelegateA.setOwner has no caller check; DelegateA.owner and DelegateB.guardian both occupy slot 0, so a 7702 account redelegating A->B reinterprets the stale owner value as guardian.
findings.impact: Anyone hijacks the account owner; redelegation yields an unintended guardian (uninitialized-delegate hazard).
findings.rootCause: Missing auth on a state setter plus colliding storage layouts across delegates.
findings.recommendation: Authorize setOwner and standardize a namespaced storage layout (ERC-7201) across all delegates, re-initializing on redelegation.
